title: Playboy Magazine March 1972 Michael Crichton Saul Alinsky Grateful Dead
conditionDescription: Pre-owned vintage issue. Cover shows toning and light soiling with edge wear, and a small chip and creasing at the lower left corner. Spine intact. No mailing label. Please review the photos for exact condition. The centerfold has not been separately verified - please ask before buying if that matters to you.
descriptionText:
Vintage Playboy Magazine, March 1972 issue. Cover price one dollar.

Features:
- The opening installment of a serialized sci-fi thriller by Michael Crichton, billed on the cover as the author of "The Andromeda Strain"
- The Playboy Interview with Saul Alinsky, the community organizer behind "Rules for Radicals." Alinsky died in June of the same year, which makes this one of the last long interviews he gave
- Tuning in on the Grateful Dead
- Peter ("Joe") Boyle lampoons motorcycle movies in "Snow's Angels"
- Bruce Jay Friedman covers and uncovers a beauty contest
- Playboy previews "Savages," a far-out flick
- A visit with the magnifique Dominique Sanda
- "Aerospaced Out" by Senator Alan Cranston
- Sokol's art gallery

Bottle-and-corkscrew cover.

The back cover carries a 1972 Viceroy cigarette ad, "Get a taste of what it's all about," shot at a drag strip.

Condition: pre-owned, complete issue with normal signs of age and storage.
